To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the neutron's electromagnetic form factors and cross sections are sensitive to the pion cloud, and that the chiral symmetry breaking scale is 4πFπ = 1 GeV.

the chiral structure of the nucleon is revealed in the electromagnetic form factors and that this is the result of a nonperturbative, nontrivial interplay between the pion cloud and the quarks and gluons of the nucleon.

(1) the neutron electric form factor at large momentum transfer is dominated by pionic short-distance correlations, (2) the neutron magnetic form factor at large-momentum transfer is also dominated by pionic correlations, and (3) the neutron magnetic polarizability, a quantity which measures its sensitivity to virtual photon exchange, is dominated by pion exchange.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the structure of the nucleon, the neutron, the nucleus and the atom.
the chiral structure of the nucleon.
the structure of the nucleon and its excited states.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the neutron is not a point particle and that its electromagnetic form factors and response to photons and leptons are driven by the excitation of its cloud of virtual pions.
the neutron is a chiral object, and the chiral properties of the neutron's structure are revealed in electron and gamma ray scattering experiments.

, in the case of the neutron, the pion cloud plays an absolutely central role in determining the response to low-momentum transfer probes, but is only a minor component of the structure at large momentum transfer.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
we are beginning to understand the chiral structure of the nucleon, and we have a reasonable understanding of how to extract it from experimental data.
the pion cloud is a dominant component of the neutron's response to electromagnetic probes at low momentum transfer, but it is not the only component.
we find a strong pion-cloud component to the neutron's electromagnetic response, and that this component is consistent with expectations from chiral symmetry.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the pion cloud's response is not simply a small correction to a short-distance structure.
, in a variety of cases, the pion cloud is a dominant contributor to the neutron response, and its influence can be isolated by a careful analysis of the data.
the neutron is an ideal laboratory for studying the chiral structure of QCD, and that this can be done with precision using existing and planned electron and photon facilities.
